title: The frontend's notification list is titled "Import notification service | Import notification service" in the browser; DR1 titles the same page "Dashboard".

finding.frontend: Both dashboard captures carry the browser title "Import notification service | Import notification service". The service name is printed twice because the page supplies the service name as its own title (`src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:2`) and the shared layout then appends the service name to whatever the page supplied (`src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:17`). Every other frontend screen names itself properly in the same slot — "Declaration", "Overview", "Upload documents" — so the front door is the one page whose tab, history entry and screen-reader page announcement say nothing about what the page is.
finding.prototype: DR1 sets the same page's title to "Dashboard" (`app/views/dashboard.html:12`), which the layout renders as "Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK". DR1's heading on that page is "Import notification service", the same words the frontend uses, so the difference is confined to the title.
finding.difference: Give the dashboard a page title of its own, distinct from the heading. DR1's word for it is "Dashboard". One string, in the dashboard's copy file; the heading stays as it is on both sides. The Welsh copy file needs the equivalent string.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a captured frontend dashboard whose browser title names the page rather than repeating the service name.
